# 4 Ezra Chapter 6 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 6:6 — God's first-person creative claim

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "then I thought it over, and these things were-made through-me" | Literal Latin cogitavi |
| LOGOS | "then I considered these things, and they all were made through me" | More natural |
| PNEUMA | "I planned all of this, and it was made through me" | Simplifies elegantly |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Then I considered these things, and they were all made through me" (LOGOS). Preserves the reflective aspect of cogitavi.

---

## 6:9 — Esau/Jacob typology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Esau-is-the-end-of-this-age, and Jacob-is-the-beginning" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "Esau is the end of this age, and Jacob is the beginning of the age that follows" | Full parallel |
| PNEUMA | "Esau is the end of this age. Jacob is the beginning of the one that follows." | Same, split into sentences |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS rendering — keeping the single sentence preserves the literary parallelism.

---

## 6:22 — premature births as eschatological sign

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "women-with-child shall-bring-forth untimely children-of-three-and-four-months, and they-shall-live and-be-quickened" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "pregnant women shall bring forth untimely children at three and four months, and these shall live and spring up" | Natural |
| PNEUMA | "Pregnant women will give birth prematurely at three and four months, and those children will live and grow up" | Clear modern |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Pregnant women shall bring forth untimely children at three and four months, and these shall live and grow up" — "grow up" (PNEUMA) is clearer than "spring up" (LOGOS) for viviscentur.

---

## 6:29 — "grasshoppers" / "locusts"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "as-locusts" | Earlier chapters used "locusts" |
| LOGOS | "like grasshoppers" | Alternative translation of quasi locustae |
| PNEUMA | "like a swarm of grasshoppers" | Adds "swarm" for vividness |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Like grasshoppers" (LOGOS). Both are valid; "grasshoppers" is slightly more natural in this lament context.

---

## 6:57 — sevenfold light for the righteous

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the light-of-the-sun seven-times-as-bright" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "the light of the sun seven times as bright" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the sun will shine with seven times its normal brightness" | Rephrased |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The light of the sun seven times as bright" (LOGOS/EMET). The most direct rendering of lux solis septuplum.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
